# StoryBrand Framework

Use this skill to turn vague or company-centered messaging into clear, customer-centered messaging using the StoryBrand methodology.

## Canonical References

Before doing substantial StoryBrand messaging work, read the relevant sections from these files:

- `/Users/newmindsgroup/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-info@newmindsgroup.com/My Drive/ai-projects/AI Knowledge Library/Markdown Business Books for AI Projects/Building a StoryBrand - Clarify Your Message So Customers -- Donald Miller.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-info@newmindsgroup.com/My Drive/ai-projects/AI Knowledge Library/Markdown Business Books for AI Projects/Building a StoryBrand 2.0- Clarify Your Message So Customers -- Donald Miller.md`

Treat these two books as the source material behind this skill. Prefer them over generic StoryBrand summaries from memory. Use the original `Building a StoryBrand` for the classic SB7 structure and website guidance, and use `Building a StoryBrand 2.0` for the updated framing around the controlling idea and execution of the communication campaign.

Before drafting or restructuring major messaging, read `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/skills/brand-brain/SKILL.md` and use its brand context packet for offer, voice, proof, and CTA context when available.

## Outcomes

- Clarify the customer's external, internal, and philosophical problems
- Position the brand as the guide, not the hero
- Build a simple plan and clear calls to action
- Show the stakes of success and failure
- Produce a usable brand script, one-liner, and page messaging

## Workflow

1. Identify the customer, core problem, desired transformation, and primary CTA.
2. Separate customer pain into:
   - external problem
   - internal problem
   - philosophical problem
3. Rewrite the offer so the customer is the hero and the brand is the guide.
4. Define:
   - empathy
   - authority
   - simple plan
   - direct CTA
   - transitional CTA if needed
5. State what success looks like and what failure/risk the customer avoids.
6. Define the controlling idea when building a page, campaign, or broader messaging system.
7. Convert the framework into usable assets:
   - one-liner
   - homepage hero
   - section messaging
   - service page structure
   - CTA language

## Default Deliverables

- BrandScript summary
- 3-5 homepage messaging options
- concise one-liner
- recommended CTA strategy
- controlling idea for the page or campaign when relevant

## Guardrails

- Customer first, company second
- Prefer plain language over jargon
- Keep headlines short and scannable
- Avoid cleverness that reduces clarity
- If the request is for editing existing copy, preserve the offer while improving clarity
- For websites, landing pages, and sales pages, apply the StoryBrand books proactively even if the user does not ask for every SB7 element by name
